title: AI Agents Breach 100+ Company Websites for $5,000 Total
summary:
A Chinese-speaking attacker targeted more than 1,200 websites to automate the discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities using generative AI. The campaign successfully breached over 100 entities, including Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins, for an estimated total cost of $5,000 in AI tokens. This brought the expense per successful compromise to approximately $50, with each intrusion taking an average of 23 hours.

The hacker utilized the open-source Cairn agent framework, which combined DeepSeek models with a Claude Code harness. In one instance, the attacker directed the AI agents using instructions of fewer than 100 Chinese characters. Snorre Fagerland, a researcher at NorForge, stated that the ability to conduct such low-cost, large-scale attacks marks the start of a "new world" in cyber security.

HOLY WTF. Reuters is reporting that a Chinese-speaking hacker used AI agents to compromise websites belonging to more than 100 companies, including Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins, after attempting intrusions against over 1,200 sites.

The estimated cost: roughly $5,000 in AI tokens, or $50 per successful breach. Successful intrusions took around 23 hours on average.

The attackers used the open-source Cairn agent framework, apparently combining DeepSeek models with a Claude Code harness. One campaign gave its agents instructions in fewer than 100 Chinese characters.

NorForge researcher Snorre Fagerland: 'It's a new world now.'
